cultural.how: Plant well-sprouted cloves in early October at 20 cm between rows and 10 cm between plants; harvest around the first week of May.

cultural.summary: The only HP garlic with some tolerance!
cultural.how: Kandaghat Selection was moderately resistant (15.6% severity) in Nauni screening; no variety is immune.

cultural.summary: The fungus lives on leftover leaves!
cultural.how: Collect and burn (or bury deep) diseased residue after harvest, rotate 2-3 years with non-host crops (cereals), keep drains open and avoid dense planting.

In Sirmaur and Solan, 24-48% of plants were affected. Copper gave only about 21% inhibition in the lab, and the best HP field control was a synthetic fungicide. Rely on early sowing, tolerant variety, residue removal and spacing.

biological.how: Treat cloves with Trichoderma harzianum at 10 g per kg cloves before planting.
biological.evidence: Dharwad garlic trial (not HP); the best schedule there also included two fungicide sprays.

cultural.how: Reduce plant density, remove diseased leaves and residue, and favour lower-rust types: rust ranged 11-32% across 35 genotypes at Nauni, lowest in LGC-3 (11%).
cultural.evidence: UHF Nauni genotype trial; a wider-spacing result is from Pakistan, not HP.

cultural.summary: The fungus lives on leftover leaves!
cultural.how: Collect and burn (or bury deep) diseased residue after harvest, rotate 2-3 years with non-host crops (cereals), keep drains open and avoid dense planting.

cultural.summary: No natural control for rust was found!
cultural.how: No natural spray with evidence against garlic rust was found. Reduce spread with spacing and sanitation and ask your KVK about options if leaves are drying early.
cultural.evidence: Searched UHF Nauni, ICAR and NIPHM sources.

cultural.summary: These soil fungi last for years!
cultural.how: Rotate 4-5 years with cereals, use disease-free fields, avoid injuring plants during hoeing, keep drainage good, and solarize with clear polythene for 30 days in summer.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM onion package (basal and white rot rows merged). HP survey: 2.1% at Nauni to 30% at Lanacheta, Sirmaur.

cultural.summary: Yellowing starts at the leaf tips and the roots rot!
cultural.how: Look for yellowing and dying leaves, rotten roots and white fluffy growth at the bulb base. Pull affected plants gently with the soil and destroy them away from the field.
cultural.evidence: Photograph the whole plant, since the leaf alone can look like Stemphylium or drought.

biological.how: Treat cloves with Trichoderma harzianum at 10 g per kg cloves before planting.
biological.evidence: Dharwad garlic trial (not HP). A Nauni pot study reported about 61-63% white-rot reduction with Trichoderma, but no dose was retrieved.

cultural.summary: Two tall rows around the plot slow thrips!
cultural.how: Sow two rows of maize around the plot, avoid following onion/garlic with onion/garlic or cabbage, tomato or cucumber, and plant the new crop upwind of older plantings.

cultural.summary: Too much urea makes soft, disease-prone leaves!
cultural.how: Use only the recommended nitrogen and phosphorus; excess nitrogen makes the crop succulent and also increases thrips.

cultural.summary: Water on leaves knocks thrips back!
cultural.how: Overhead sprinkler irrigation reduces thrips more than drip or surface irrigation; avoid crop stress and thin patchy stands.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM onion package. Thrips peak in April on rabi onion at Palampur.

biological.how: Hang 4-5 blue sticky traps per acre just above the crop.
Spray Beauveria bassiana, Metarhizium anisopliae or Lecanicillium lecanii at 60 g in 10 L water (0.007%), covering both sides of the leaves.
biological.frequency: At first thrips; repeat after 10-15 days
biological.evidence: Navsari garlic trial (not HP): moderate control only.

botanical.summary: The best-value spray in the garlic thrips trial!
botanical.how: Mix 500 g neem seed kernel extract in 10 L water (5%) and spray, covering both sides of the leaves.
botanical.frequency: At first thrips; repeat after 10-15 days
botanical.evidence: Navsari garlic trial (not HP): thrips fell to 6-8 per plant against 18-25 in untreated plots, and yield rose from 40 to 62.5 q/ha.
